title: Enterprise network compatibility signal harness + FastPass lane for private deployments
creator: Priya Narang
description: Goal: build an automated 'signal harness' that aggregates lightweight network compatibility probes, upgrade-readiness checks, and packaging signals to score incoming Private/VPC/on-prem requests and surface a FastPass lane for low-friction approvals. Scope includes: (1) define probe set (eg. egress rules, outbound TLS, port reachability, proxy auth flows, NAT behavior), (2) acceptance thresholds and risk bucketing, (3) automated routing: self-serve checklist vs concierge onboarding vs blocked for architecture changes, (4) UX surface in Console intake with transparent signal feedback to customers and SSO-friendly reporting for security teams, (5) runbook and rollback play for upgrades in airgapped environments.
comments: 2025-03-18: Initial intake — multiple enterprise customers requested faster triage for VPC/airgapped installs; current manual intake causing 7–12 day wait for low-risk requests.
2025-03-19: PM/Design sync — agreed to surface probe results in Console intake; design will mock a compact signal summary and 'FastPass eligibility' badge.

2025-03-20: Eng feasibility — Liam: we can run non-invasive probes from staging probes-nodes and collect deterministic signals, estimate 5 points. Need ENG to add a short-lived probe runner behind customer-provided connectors for airgapped cases.

2025-03-22: Security review kickoff — Elena: must avoid sending customer secrets; probes must be deterministic and one-way; KMS handshake simulated where HSM integration required is flagged as 'manual'.

2025-03-24: Stakeholder alignment — agreed thresholds: Low-risk if all core probes pass and no outbound custom ports required; Medium if additional port exceptions needed; High if NAT/proxy auth blocks or HSM/KMS on-prem required. FastPass to auto-approve Low-risk with emailed pre-approved SLA and 72h automated provisioning window.
acceptance_criteria: Signal harness prototype executes a defined set of 8 probes against a sample customer environment and produces deterministic pass/fail outputs.
Console intake shows signal summary and FastPass eligibility badge for at least two documented customer scenarios.

Routing policy implemented: Low-risk -> automatic FastPass provisioning API call; Medium -> routed to concierge with prefilled diagnostic payload; High -> routed to architecture review and blocked until manual remediation.
Security review signoff confirming probes do not transmit customer secrets and that HSM/KMS cases are flagged and never automated for FastPass.
Runbook and SLA artifacts published in Confluence and linked in Console for customers who receive FastPass approval.
decisions: We will prioritize non-invasive deterministic network probes (port scans against known hostnames, TLS handshake checks) over any probes that require credentials.
FastPass will only auto-approve 'Low-risk' bucket; any HSM, custom root CA, or strict airgap will require manual concierge due to compliance risk.
Weighting: connectivity + TLS + port reachability = 70% of score; proxy auth/NAT oddities = 30% and can block FastPass if failing.
Expose probe results to customers in a single-line pass/fail with an expandable details panel to reduce support noise.
next_steps: Finalize probe list and concrete test payloads (ENG/SEC/PM) by 2025-03-28
Design deliverables: high-fidelity intake mock and notification copy by 2025-03-27
Eng: spike to run probes from staging nodes and validate deterministic outputs (owner: Liam) — complete by 2025-03-31
Security: complete quick threat model and signoff on probe runner by 2025-04-02
Prepare FastPass policy doc and legal/comms template for auto-approvals by 2025-04-05
notes: This ticket intentionally focuses on low-friction triage to reclaim manual engineering time and reduce time-to-first-run for enterprise customers whose environments are compatible. We must ensure transparency to customers to prevent false trust in FastPass; every auto-approval will include an audit trail and ability to revoke provisioning within a 7-day safe window.
